eventMetadata.context_description: Forecast models from sources like AccuWeather and the National Meteorological Service indicate a June 9 high near 21–22°C for Mexico City, shaped by the city’s 2,240-meter elevation and the onset of the rainy season. Persistent cloud cover and scattered afternoon thundershowers suppress peak heating, keeping surface temperatures below the long-term June average of 24–25°C. Trader consensus around 20–21°C reflects uncertainty in exact timing and intensity of convection, which can shift daily maxima by 1–2°C. Historical analogs show early-June highs declining as moisture influx increases, while any break in cloudiness could push readings toward 23°C. Updated model runs and official observations through the day remain the key variables ahead of market resolution.
